title: Impact of Atrial Fibrillation Prediction Model on Prescribing Oral Anti-Coagulation in Patients With Cryptogenic Stroke
official: Prediction of Atrial Fibrillation in Patients With Embolic Stroke of Unknown Source
summary:
Stroke is a major cause of disability and the second leading cause of death in adults. Some strokes are linked to atrial fibrillation (AF), a type of irregular heartbeat. When AF is found, doctors usually prescribe blood-thinning medicines to help prevent another stroke. If AF is not found, patients are usually treated with antiplatelet medicines, such as aspirin.

However, AF can be difficult to detect. Because of this, doctors may not know which treatment is best.

Our research team has developed computer programs that analyze a normal electrocardiogram (EKG) and predict whether a person may develop AF in the future. These programs have been shown to be highly accurate.

The goal of this study is to see how sharing these prediction results affects treatment decisions made by patients who have had an embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS) and their neurologist. An ESUS is a type of stroke where the exact cause cannot be identified.

Participants in the study will have their normal EKG analyzed using the prediction program. Researchers will then evaluate whether providing these results to the neurologist influences decisions about the patient's care.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient presenting with embolic stroke of unclear source.
* Age at least 18 years.
* Patients will be enrolled within 30 days of stroke.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior history of AF
* Stroke can be attributed to cancer, hypercoagulable state, or large artery non-stenotic plaque
* Contraindication to OAC or antiplatelet therapy, including the presence of hemorrhagic stroke
* Patient is already on OAC
* Patient had prior procedure or surgery to exclude or excise the left atrial appendage
* Patient unable or unwilling to provide written informed consent to participate in research
